research_metadata.scope: Publisher-authored App Store listings and developer websites only; claims are paraphrased.
research_metadata.ranking_caveat: The supplied US and Mexico search observations describe web search results on 2026-10-20, not native App Store charts, editorial rankings, or an objective best-app ranking. Do not present them as native iPhone rank or proof of being #1.

apps.name: Unit Converter - Best Unit App

claims.claim: The listing describes a broad unit converter with 20 categories, including angle, area, currency, computer data, network speed, energy, force, fuel mileage, length, clothing sizes, pressure, speed, temperature, time, torque, volume, and weight/mass.
The listing says it supports 155 world currencies and downloads exchange rates once per day when the app is opened; it explicitly says an internet connection is required for currency-rate downloads.
The App Store labels it Free with In-App Purchases. Its version-history description says search, favorites, fractions, compound units, a calculator, and dark/light mode were added.

known_limitations: Do not infer offline currency conversion from the listing; it says currency-rate downloads require internet.
apps.source_notes: Publisher site is listed by the App Store, but the sourced feature claims above come from the current App Store description/version history.

apps.name: My Currency Converter & Rates

claims.claim: The listing focuses on currency conversion and describes support for 150+ fiat currencies plus Bitcoin, Litecoin, and Dogecoin.
The listing says rates update automatically, users can invert the pair, conversion updates while typing, and the current exchange rate can be viewed.

The description explicitly says the app can show currency value without an internet connection. A user review on the same App Store listing says offline use is fully functional; treat the review as user testimony, not a publisher guarantee of rate freshness.
The listing labels the app Free and says this version is ad-supported.

known_limitations: The listing does not specify how often rates refresh or which rate data remains available offline; do not claim a freshness interval.
apps.source_notes: Avoid relying on reviews for feature comparisons except as clearly labeled user testimony.

apps.name: Converter: Units & Currencies (also observed localized as Convertidor Lite)

claims.claim: The listing describes 25+ categories and 450+ units, including scientific, everyday, cooking, measurement, and currency categories.
The listing says it supports 150+ currencies and 24 languages.
The App Store lists it as Free and says it is designed for iPad as well as supporting iPhone; the listed compatibility requirement is iOS 10.0 or later.

known_limitations: The listing's visible feature description does not specify currency update cadence, offline behavior, charts, widgets, or a calculator. Silence is not evidence that a feature is absent.
apps.source_notes: The current App Store version history shown is old (last displayed release in 2019); feature counts reflect the live listing text, not an independent test.

apps.name: Xe Money Transfer & Currency

claims.claim: The App Store positions Xe as a currency converter, live exchange-rate tracker, and international money-transfer app; it describes transfers to 190+ countries in 130+ currencies, with availability varying by region and eligibility.

The App Store listing documents live rates, conversion, real-time FX movement tracking, and rate alerts. Xe's publisher FAQ says setting an in-app Rate Alert requires registration and email verification.
The App Store version history says the currency-converter home-screen widget returned with live mid-market rates and later updates mention improved exchange-rate charts.
The App Store labels Xe Free. The publisher's iOS/Android product page also describes live rates, rate alerts, and viewing historical data; use the App Store as the source for iPhone-specific claims.

known_limitations: Position Xe as a currency-market and transfer option, not a general measurement-unit converter.
Transfer destinations, payment methods, fees, availability, and account services vary by region and eligibility.
Do not claim offline behavior; it is not specified in the listing.
apps.source_notes: Keep comparisons focused on the published feature set; do not assert that Xe lacks general-unit conversion solely because the App Store copy centers on currencies and transfers.

publisher_authored_comparison_framing.recommended_intro: The right converter depends on what you convert most: broad measurement coverage, quick travel currency checks, or currency tracking and transfers.

selection_suggestions.use_case: A single app for frequent unit conversions plus currencies and calculator-style input
selection_suggestions.reason: The supplied product facts combine 72 categories, 685 non-currency units, currency/crypto/metals, history, favorites, and an expression calculator.

selection_suggestions.use_case: A large catalog of measurement categories and languages
selection_suggestions.reason: Its listing claims 25+ categories, 450+ units, 150+ currencies, and 24 languages.

selection_suggestions.use_case: Straightforward travel currency conversion with offline use described
selection_suggestions.reason: Its listing centers on pair conversion, auto-updating rates, and use without internet; it also includes major cryptocurrencies.

selection_suggestions.use_case: A broad unit-and-currency app with built-in calculator features
selection_suggestions.reason: Its listing describes 20 unit categories, daily currency-rate downloads, favorites, fractions, compound units, and calculator features.

selection_suggestions.use_case: Currency market monitoring, alerts, and international transfers
selection_suggestions.reason: Its App Store listing emphasizes live FX rates, alerts, exchange-rate charts, a currency widget, and transfers.

editorial_guardrails: Describe these as editorial picks by use case, not an objective or independently tested #1 ranking.
Avoid saying a competitor lacks an unmentioned feature; state only documented features and explain where its listing is silent.

Avoid the phrase 'App Store top-ranked' based on web search results. If mentioning search visibility, identify the search engine, query, market, and observation date, and explain that it is not App Store chart ranking.
Before publication, recheck live App Store descriptions, price labels, compatibility, and any time-sensitive rate-update claims.
